observation.visible_scene: Night sky over a silhouetted city skyline with scattered lights, a dark bridge/parapet in the lower-left foreground and faint water reflection below. A steady white plume (fountain-like spray) rises from the horizon near the center throughout the clip. Above it, a ring of small blue-white spark dots surrounds a brightening white core, and later a separate white petal/flower-shaped burst forms higher in the sky. A faint isolated dot sits high near the top center in every frame.
visible_changes: The wide ring of blue-white dots centered around (460,380) is brightest and most spread out in frames 1-3 and gradually dims and contracts through frame 21, while its central white core grows from a faint point (frame 1) into a small bright burst (frames 6-21).
The white ground-level plume near (460,440) persists with roughly constant height and position across all frames, only subtly changing shape.
At frame 22 a new bright starburst with radiating streaks appears higher, around (465,290), distinct from the fading blue ring below.

From frame 23 to frame 41 that upper burst resolves into a flower/peony shape of white petals that steadily expands in size and brightens, with the petal arrangement rotating slightly; the blue ring below it continues to fade and is nearly gone by the end.
The high faint dot near (465,240) stays at the same image position in every frame, and the skyline/bridge do not shift, indicating a fixed camera.
outside_clip_unknowns: How and when the firework shells were launched and what preceded the initial blue-dot burst.
Whether the persistent white plume is a water fountain or a ground-level firework effect, and what causes it.
What happens after frame 41 (whether the flower burst fully blooms, fades, or new shells fire).
uncertain_details: The exact nature of the steady white plume (water vs. firework smoke) cannot be confirmed from the frames.
The identity of the static high dot (lingering ember, star, or artifact) is unclear.
Minor apparent motion of the burst patterns is expansion/rotation of the firework itself, not camera movement, but slight handheld jitter cannot be fully excluded.
